title: Getting Started Route
description: The onboard frontend module shall serve an authenticated getting-started page reachable by both student and admin roles.
rationale: New users of either role need a single, bookmarkable orientation page reachable without hunting through the application.

title: Getting Started Nav Link
description: The onboard frontend module shall render a Getting Started navigation link in the persistent navigation bar for all authenticated users.
rationale: Orientation guidance must be reachable from any authenticated page so users can consult it at any point in their workflow.

title: Student Orientation Steps
description: The onboard frontend module shall display a seven-step student orientation sequence on /getting-started for users with role student.
rationale: Students need role-appropriate guidance covering every stage of the learning workflow from consent through grade receipt.

title: Admin Orientation Steps
description: The onboard frontend module shall display a four-step admin orientation sequence on /getting-started for users with role admin.
rationale: Admins need role-appropriate guidance covering user management, system configuration, audit oversight, and course monitoring.

title: Student Step 1 — AI Consent
description: The onboard frontend module shall present consent acceptance as the first student orientation step.
rationale: Consent is a gate that must be completed before any other student workflow step; it must be first in the sequence.

title: Student Step 2 — Create Course with Topic
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe creating a course by entering a non-empty topic as the second student orientation step.
rationale: The backend course creation endpoint requires a topic field; the orientation must reflect this exact field name and requirement.

title: Student Step 3 — Intake Chat
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe the intake chat with the AI agent as the third student orientation step.
rationale: Intake chat is the first substantive AI interaction; students must know it follows course creation.

title: Student Step 4 — Syllabus Approval
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe reviewing and approving the AI-generated syllabus as the fourth student orientation step.
rationale: Syllabus approval is a required gate before schedule agreement; students must understand they control this checkpoint.

title: Student Step 5 — Generated Sections
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe navigating the AI-generated course sections as the fifth student orientation step.
rationale: After schedule agreement the content generation pipeline runs; students must know sections will appear automatically.

title: Student Step 6 — Homework Submission
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe submitting homework assignments as the sixth student orientation step.
rationale: Homework submission is the primary graded activity; students need orientation on how and where to submit.

title: Student Step 7 — Grades and Badges
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe viewing grades and earned badges as the seventh student orientation step.
rationale: Grades and badges are the terminal outcome of the course workflow; students need to know where to find them.

title: Admin Step 1 — User Management
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe the user management view as the first admin orientation step.
rationale: User provisioning is the first administrative task in a new deployment; it must be the first orientation step.

title: Admin Step 2 — System Configuration Guide
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe system configuration with a link to docs/guides/admin-configuration.md as the second admin orientation step.
rationale: Admins must be directed to the configuration guide document before adjusting the thirteen system_config keys to avoid misconfiguration.

title: Admin Step 3 — Audit Log
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe the audit log view and integrity verification as the third admin orientation step.
rationale: Audit log review is a periodic oversight obligation; admins must be oriented to the view and its verification action.

title: Admin Step 4 — Course Oversight
description: The onboard frontend module shall describe the course oversight view as the fourth admin orientation step.
rationale: Course oversight enables admins to monitor the student pipeline and diagnose issues; it is the last orientation step after setup tasks.

title: Admin Configuration Guide Document
description: The onboard frontend module shall include a maintained guide at docs/guides/admin-configuration.md covering all thirteen system_config keys.
rationale: Admins require reference documentation for each system_config key, its validation rules, and audit impact before making configuration changes.

title: Config Guide — All Thirteen Keys Documented
description: The onboard frontend module shall document all thirteen system_config keys in docs/guides/admin-configuration.md.
rationale: The thirteen keys are: agent_retry_limit, correction_loop_max_iterations, per_student_token_limit, late_penalty_rate, homework_weight, project_weight, session_inactivity_seconds, account_lockout_seconds, max_upload_bytes, content_generation_timeout_seconds, audit_retention_days, notification_retention_days, and consent_version. Omitting any key leaves admins without complete reference.

title: Config Guide — Validation Rules Per Key
description: The onboard frontend module shall document the validation rule for each system_config key in docs/guides/admin-configuration.md.
rationale: Each key has a distinct constraint enforced by the backend; documenting these constraints prevents rejected PATCH requests and accidental misconfiguration.

title: Config Guide — Audit Impact Documented
description: The onboard frontend module shall document how configuration changes are recorded in the audit log in docs/guides/admin-configuration.md.
rationale: Admins must understand that each config change produces an audit entry so they can plan changes and review their effects in the audit log.
